Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: GIMTEL (national switch) is constituted “under the aegis” of the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie (BCM) ([GIMTEL](https://gimtel.mr/fr/missions)). BCM is also a member of GIMTEL, and BCM’s Governor participated in the launch of an interoperable mobile payment project implemented by GIMTEL ([GBM Banque](https://www.gbm-banque.com/en/actualites/bcm-new-agreement-implementation-interoperable-mobile-payment-project)). This indicates central bank involvement beyond regulation, with governance/oversight and participation in the scheme.
revision_notes: Both originally cited sources were fetched and verified as accurate and current. GIMTEL's own site confirms it was created in May 2005 under the aegis of the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie (BCM) as a Groupement d'Intérêt Économique whose members include BCM, Mauripost and the commercial banks, and that BCM sits on GIMTEL's conseil d'administration (board). A October 2024 news report (Sahara Media) confirms the Governor of BCM personally launched a further phase of payment-infrastructure reform (interbank e-wallet interoperability) delivered through GIMTEL, describing it as part of BCM strategy, while GIMTEL's own director general (not BCM staff) runs day-to-day operations. This is consistent with Board Representation (4) rather than Direct Operation (5). Score confirmed unchanged at 4.
revised_comments: GIMTEL, Mauritania's interbank card and payments switch, was established in May 2005 under the aegis of the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie (BCM) as a Groupement d'Intérêt Économique whose members include the BCM, Mauripost and the country's commercial banks. BCM holds a board seat on GIMTEL's governing council, and its Governor has personally launched major payment-infrastructure reforms delivered through GIMTEL, including the 2021 interoperable mobile wallet project and the October 2024 launch of interbank e-wallet interoperability, both framed explicitly as part of BCM strategy. Day-to-day operation of GIMTEL is run by its own director general rather than by the central bank directly, placing BCM's role at board representation rather than direct operation.

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: Global Findex figures cited by UNCDF indicate mobile money account ownership was about 4% of adults in 2018, which is <20% ([UNCDF Policy Accelerator](https://policyaccelerator.uncdf.org/whats-new/mauritania-regulatory-framework)). No newer nationally representative active-user share was located, so the score reflects the latest cited penetration evidence.
revision_notes: The originally cited UNCDF source was fetched and confirmed accurate for its 2018 reference point (mobile money accounts ~4% of adults) but is now stale. The World Bank's live Global Findex data portal (fetched directly) shows account ownership at a financial institution or with a mobile-money provider (% of population aged 15+) for Mauritania at 27.31% for 2024, drawn from the newly released Global Findex 2025 database. This is a broader measure than the variable's strict definition (active use of digital payments in the past 90 days, rather than account ownership), and no Mauritania-specific past-90-day active-usage figure could be located, but it is the best available authoritative proxy per the metadata guidance and it moves the country from the <20% band into the 20-49% band. Score revised from 1 to 2; year-confidence set to medium given the proxy/definition mismatch.
revised_comments: The most recent Global Findex data (fieldwork 2024, published in the World Bank's Global Findex 2025 database) show account ownership at a financial institution or with a mobile-money provider standing at 27.31% of the adult population (15+) in Mauritania, up from single-digit mobile money account penetration in 2018. This measures account ownership rather than active use of digital payments in the past 90 days specifically, but it is the best available nationally representative proxy and places usage in the 20-49% band.
